sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:112198
Court No. - 81
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 2091 of 2023

Appellant :- Rajiya
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Appellant :- Vishvendra Singh

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Heard Shri Vishvendra Singh, learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant appeal under Section 14-A(1) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed by the appellant- Rajiya with the prayer to allow the present criminal appeal and to quash the impugned charge sheet no. 505-A/2020 dated 09.03.2021 and its consequential summoning order dated 28.07.2021 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST) Act, Agra in Special Session Trial No.
106 of 2021 (State of U.P. vs. Rajiya), arising out of Case Crime No. 439 of 2020, under Sections 323, 365, 376-D, 506, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Shahganj,
District Agra.

Learned counsel for the appellant while drawing the attention of this Court towards the impugned order of date 28.07.2021 as well as charge sheet filed against the appellant, vehemently submits that the Special Court has committed manifest illegality in summoning the appellant to face trial for the various offences including Section 376-D of the I.P.C., as there was no sufficient material available in the case diary on the basis of which the appellant may be summoned to face trial.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that appellant is a lady and, therefore, may never be an accused of committing rape, as defined under Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is also submitted that there is material contradiction in the statement of the victim/prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161, 164 Cr.P.C. as well as in the additional statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Thus, the impugned order is suffering from inherent illegality and the same is required to be set-aside.

Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that no illegality or to say any irregularity has been committed by the Special Court in taking cognizance and issuing process as well as by the investigating officer in submitting the charge sheet, as at the stage of summoning only a primafacie case is required to be seen.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record and keeping in view the order intended to be passed, the service of notice to the opposite party no.2 is hereby dispensed with.
Perusal of the record would reveal that F.I.R. of the instant case has been lodged by the opposite party no.2 alleging various allegations against co-accused Ashiq @ Asif.

However, in the statement of the victim/prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161, 164 Cr.P.C. as well as in the additional statement recorded by the investigating officer under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim has levelled allegations against the instant appellant, which primafacie attracts the provision of Section 120-B I.P.C.
The truthfulness or the falsity of the statements of the victims or any other witness may only be tested during the course of trial.

However, on the basis of minor contradictions appearing in the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the same cannot form the sole basis for quashing all the proceedings pending against the appellant.

Thus, for the reasons aforesaid, I do not find any illegality so far as the summoning of the instant appellant is concerned and, therefore, impugned order whereby the appellant has been summoned,
is hereby affirmed.
In result, the appeal lacks merit and is dismissed as such.

However, all the grounds which have been taken by the appellant before this Court may be taken by her at the time of disposal of her plea of bail, if bail has already not been secured by the appellant and in case the grounds, which have been taken in the instant appeal are placed before the Special Court at the stage of considering her plea of bail, the trial Court shall pay due regard to all the submissions which may be raised before it at the time of considering plea of bail of the appellant.
Order Date :- 22.5.2023
